rows.title: CT ends longstanding dispute with federal tax officials over big state pensions
rows.standfirst: Comptroller Kevin P. Lembo says the agreement preserves the tax exempt status of the state pension fund.

rows.title: Lamont: Full reopening of bars in mid-July must ‘take a pause’
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont all but shut the door Thursday on a full-scale reopening of Connecticut bars in mid-July.

rows.title: A Magical Merry-Go-Round, hot yoga and, oh yeah, that much-needed haircut
Some CT companies borrowed up to $10 million in forgivable funds from Paycheck Protection Program
rows.standfirst: Connecticut borrowers included law firms, manufacturers and Choate, who says it returned the money.

rows.title: A billion in federal funds flies out the door … and more is needed
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont’s administration expects to finish divvying up Connecticut’s $1.4 billion share of the Coronavirus Relief Fund next month.

rows.title: New Haven’s effort to help the hardest hit: minority-owned small businesses
rows.standfirst: Businesses owned by minorities and women suffered disproportionately during the COVID-19 pandemic. New Haven is trying to help.

rows.title: With COVID rates down, U.S. Census takers to begin canvassing in Hartford
rows.standfirst: Falling COVID-19 infection rates will allow the Census to start door-to-door visits in Hartford, the city with the worst self-response rate in Connecticut.

rows.title: Pandemic restricts Connecticut’s credit card; planned projects would shatter it by $2B
rows.standfirst: More than $2 billion in planned projects might have to be suspended to keep state borrowing under a tight cap.

rows.title: GOP leader: Lamont is spending when he should be hiding CT’s credit card
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont wants to spend $550 million on capital projects, a move one called “irresponsible” given CT’s fiscal woes.

rows.title: Nursing homes want more emergency beds, state funding, to continue battling COVID-19
rows.standfirst: Nursing homes want to double their emergency bed system for COVID-19 patients in anticipation of a second wave this fall.

rows.title: Pandemic, tax issues give Connecticut a chance to reset economy, strengthen the region
rows.standfirst: With the coronavirus turning many commuters into at-home workers, Connecticut has a unique chance to reset its economy.

rows.title: Bond commission approves $550 M in financing for capital projects — but partisan debate over borrowing continues
rows.standfirst: The State Bond Commission approved nearly $550 million in financing for school construction, transportation and other capital projects Tuesday.

rows.title: Gov. Lamont throws out a first pitch … to the Toronto Blue Jays
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont is trying to lure the Toronto Blue Jays to the capital city for 2020.

rows.title: As $600 weekly unemployment benefits end, a wave of evictions is expected in CT
rows.standfirst: The federal moratorium on evictions is also ending Friday, and state protections lapse soon after.

rows.title: Connecticut’s coffers have swelled — not shrunk — during COVID
rows.standfirst: Despite big deficit warnings, Connecticut’s coffers have swelled by hundreds of millions of dollars since the coronavirus struck in mid-March.

rows.title: GOP stimulus funds would relax restrictions on Connecticut’s COVID funds, but that’s little help to Lamont
rows.standfirst: While the GOP has offered to relax restrictions, it opposes new pandemic funds for state and local governments.

rows.title: A digital welcome mat for business goes live, just in time
rows.standfirst: Amid signs that COVID is stimulating economic activity in Connecticut, the state launched a new digital welcome mat.

rows.title: State regulators say they will investigate Eversource rate hike
rows.standfirst: Anticipating electric demand before and during the COVID-19 pandemic has resulted in an unwelcome surprise: massive jumps on electric bills.
